market_mood: The Iran war keeps oil, shipping and missile-defense headlines front and center, while Fed hawkishness (Waller) pushes yields up and a wave of M&A — Starbucks/Chipotle chatter, Viatris/Pacira, Crescent/Devon — dominates corporate news.
self_check: My oil and rates calls have worked far better (85% and 69%) than my M&A calls (30%), and bearish calls have outperformed bullish ones, so today I lean on the Hormuz/oil chain and a hawkish-Fed bank idea, keep merger ideas smaller, and include one bearish acquirer call.

picks.reason: Iran is vowing to block more Hormuz routes and transits are at a two-month low, which drives tanker war-risk premiums and spot rates sharply higher for crude carriers like DHT.
Houthis hit Riyadh airport with a ballistic missile and regional missile/drone attacks are escalating, which tends to drive Gulf and US demand for Patriot and air-defense interceptors.
Reports that Starbucks explored a takeover of Chipotle sent CMG up 7%; acquirers in large, unexpected deals usually get sold as investors question focus and funding.
Devon is selling its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent for $4.2B, a big cash infusion for debt paydown and buybacks that arrives while oil prices are climbing on Middle East supply fears.
Fed's Waller says more hikes are needed and long yields keep rising, which supports bank net interest income ahead of JPMorgan's Q3 report next week.
AkzoNobel is reportedly offering divestments to EU regulators to clear its purchase of Axalta, a step that raises the odds the deal closes at the agreed terms.

watchlist_notes.note: Index slipped as higher oil and higher yields pressured stocks, even as the WTO lifted its trade forecast.
Tech is the weakest sector of the past week; Samsung's record AI-driven profit is a supportive data point but hasn't lifted the group.
Dow drifting with oil-driven cost worries and hawkish Fed comments; no single Dow-specific headline today.
Only minor news — tokenized Apple shares launched by Securitize — nothing fundamental.
Named among tech firms suspended from a US immigration program, a modest headline risk against a huge AI spending backdrop.
SpaceX reportedly buying more GPUs and Samsung's record AI profit support demand, though the stock fell with tech on valuation worries.
No major news today beyond data-center supplier chatter (Generac's generator deal).
Signed a large nuclear power deal to feed data centers and is argued to be the cheapest Mag 7 name; mildly supportive.
Commentary flags its Muse AI product hitting website-access blocks, a small negative versus Google's data advantage.
No major news today; only tokenized-stock product mentions.
Rising long yields and the Oct 13 Q3 report are the near-term drivers; higher rates generally help net interest income.
Oil jumped again on Hormuz attack fears, which supports earnings, though energy has already run +3.9% this week.
War escalation supports gold, but hawkish Fed talk and higher real yields are a headwind.
Waller saying more hikes are needed keeps pressure on long bonds, though some options traders are calling a bottom after a solid 10-year auction.

top_buys.pitch: Hormuz chaos is a direct earnings windfall for crude tanker owners.
top_buys.why: Iran has vowed to block more Hormuz routes and transits have fallen to the lowest in over two months, while attack risk on tankers is rising. That combination lifts war-risk insurance, lengthens voyages around disrupted routes and pushes spot tanker rates up, which flows straight to VLCC owners like DHT. Asia is also racing to stockpile oil, adding long-haul cargo demand.
top_buys.risks: A ceasefire or de-escalation would deflate rates quickly, and tanker stocks are volatile and can give back gains in days.
top_buys.watch: Weekly VLCC spot rate prints and Hormuz transit data from Reuters.

top_buys.pitch: Missiles hitting Riyadh airport mean more orders for air-defense interceptors.
top_buys.why: The Houthis struck Riyadh airport with a ballistic missile and a plane was seen burning, the sharpest escalation yet in the Gulf. Former defense secretary Esper sees no end to the Iran war in sight, and officials are pushing space-based missile tracking. RTX makes Patriot and related interceptors and is a prime beneficiary of restocking by Gulf states and the US.
top_buys.risks: Defense primes move slowly on news and industrials have lagged the market; any peace progress would cool the theme.
top_buys.watch: New foreign military sales announcements to Gulf states and RTX's late-October earnings.

top_buys.pitch: A surprise Chipotle takeover exploration raises questions Starbucks shareholders didn't want.
top_buys.why: Reports say Starbucks has explored buying Chipotle, which sent CMG up 7% on the day. Buyers of large, strategically odd deals usually see their own shares fall as investors worry about dilution, debt and management distraction during an already difficult turnaround. Even if the deal never happens, the signal about capital allocation lingers.
top_buys.risks: Starbucks could publicly deny interest, which would quickly erase the discount; the stock is already down on the report.
top_buys.watch: Any formal statement from Starbucks and its next quarterly results in early November.

top_buys.pitch: A $4.2B asset sale hands Devon cash just as oil rallies on war risk.
top_buys.why: Devon agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets to Crescent Energy for $4.2 billion, giving it a large slug of cash to cut debt and buy back stock. Sellers in these deals often get less attention than buyers on day one, so the re-rating can unfold over weeks. Rising crude on Hormuz disruption adds a tailwind for the remaining Permian-weighted portfolio.
top_buys.risks: If oil reverses on any Middle East de-escalation, E&P shares fall regardless of the deal; investors may also question selling assets near a price peak.
top_buys.watch: Devon's capital-return update and Q3 earnings in early November.

top_buys.pitch: Hawkish Fed talk and higher yields set up a solid bank earnings season starting with JPMorgan.
top_buys.why: Fed's Waller said more hikes are needed and long-term yields stayed firm after a strong 10-year auction. Higher-for-longer rates support bank net interest income, and heavy M&A activity across the tape points to healthy investment banking fees. JPMorgan kicks off bank earnings next week, and financials have quietly outperformed over the past week.
top_buys.risks: Credit costs or a cautious outlook could overshadow good revenue, and the valuation is already premium.
top_buys.watch: JPMorgan's Q3 results on October 13 and its net interest income guidance.

summary.big_story: Escalating Iran/Houthi attacks around Hormuz and Riyadh pushed oil higher and shipping risk to wartime peaks, while hawkish Fed comments lifted yields.
summary.top_pick: DHT Holdings — crude tanker rates should keep climbing as Hormuz transits fall and war-risk premiums spike.
summary.watch: Delta's Friday morning earnings for how badly high jet fuel is biting, and any further Hormuz shipping attacks.
